title: Host acid signal controls Salmonella flagella biogenesis through CadC-YdiV axis.
authors: Wang, Weiwei; Yue, Yingying; Zhang, Min; Song, Nannan; Jia, Haihong; Dai, Yuanji; Zhang, Fengyu; Li, Cuiling; Li, Bingqing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究沙门氏菌转录因子CadC直接结合ydiV启动子DNA调控鞭毛合成，属于TF-DNA互作机制研究，但以实验为主、结构模拟为辅，AI/物理模拟方法深度有限。
abstract: Upon entering host cells, Salmonella quickly turns off flagella biogenesis to avoid recognition by the host immune system. However, it is not clear which host signal(s) Salmonella senses to initiate flagellum control. Here, we demonstrate that the acid signal can suppress flagella synthesis and motility of Salmonella, and this occurs after the transcription of master flagellar gene flhDC and depends on the anti-FlhDC factor YdiV. YdiV expression is activated after acid treatment. A global screen with ydiV promoter DNA and total protein from acid-treated Salmonella revealed a novel regulator of YdiV, the acid-related transcription factor CadC. Further studies showed that CadC(C), the DNA binding domain of CadC, directly binds to a 33 nt region of the ydiV promoter with a 0.2 muM K(D) affinity. Furthermore, CadC could separate H-NS-ydiV promoter DNA complex to form CadC-DNA complex at a low concentration. Structural simulation and mutagenesis assays revealed that H43 and W106 of CadC are essential for ydiV promoter binding. No acid-induced flagellum control phenotype was observed in cadC mutant or ydiV mutant strains, suggesting that flagellum control during acid adaption is dependent on CadC and YdiV. The intracellular survival ability of cadC mutant strain decreased significantly compared with WT strain while the flagellin expression could not be effectively controlled in the cadC mutant strain when surviving within host cells. Together, our results demonstrated that acid stress acts as an important host signal to trigger Salmonella flagellum control through the CadC-YdiV-FlhDC axis, allowing Salmonella to sense a hostile environment and regulate flagellar synthesis during infection.
abstract_zh: 进入宿主细胞后，沙门氏菌迅速关闭鞭毛生物合成，以避免被宿主免疫系统识别。然而，目前尚不清楚沙门氏菌感知何种宿主信号以启动鞭毛调控。在此，我们证明酸信号能抑制沙门氏菌的鞭毛合成和运动性，这一过程发生在主鞭毛基因flhDC转录之后，并依赖于抗FlhDC因子YdiV。酸处理后，YdiV表达被激活。通过使用ydiV启动子DNA和酸处理沙门氏菌总蛋白进行全基因组筛选，我们发现了一个新的YdiV调控因子，即酸相关转录因子CadC。进一步研究表明，CadC的DNA结合域CadC(C)直接结合ydiV启动子的33核苷酸区域，亲和力为0.2 μM K(D)。此外，CadC在低浓度下能将H-NS-ydiV启动子DNA复合物分离，形成CadC-DNA复合物。结构模拟和突变分析揭示，CadC的H43和W106对ydiV启动子结合至关重要。在cadC突变株或ydiV突变株中未观察到酸诱导的鞭毛调控表型，表明酸适应过程中的鞭毛调控依赖于CadC和YdiV。与野生型菌株相比，cadC突变株的胞内生存能力显著下降，且在宿主细胞内生存时，cadC突变株中鞭毛蛋白表达无法有效控制。综上所述，我们的结果表明，酸应激作为重要的宿主信号，通过CadC-YdiV-FlhDC轴触发沙门氏菌鞭毛调控，使沙门氏菌在感染过程中感知不利环境并调节鞭毛合成。
